text.p: Enron Corp Chairman Ken Lay on Tuesday said the company expects to generate 1998 earnings in the $2.50 to $2.60 a share range.
The lowered estimate, which Lay made on a conference call with reporters, followed a company forecast trimming its 1997 earnings estimate by $0.30 a share to $2.25 a share.
The company said interest on debt tied to its J-Block take or pay settlement will cut 1998 earnings by $0.10 a share.

Enron reported a second quarter loss of $1.71 a share, or $420 million, including $1.81 a share non-recurring charge tied to its amended J-block contract in the U.K. North Sea and a $0.30 a share charge to reflect depressed MTBE gasoline additive margins.
Second quarter income from operations, excluding the charges, was $104 million on $3.2 billion revenues compared with net income of $117 million on $3 billion revenues for the same period last year.
Lay said Enron considered selling some of its $19 billion in assets to meet forecasts of double-digit earnings for the second quarter and year.

"As we moved forward, we decided it makes more sense to continue to grow the underlying operating income at good, strong growth rates than it does to meet specific targets," he said on a conference call from London.

Before the second quarter results were released with warnings of lower earnings forecast for the year, First Call analysts expected consensus $2.40 a share earnings this year and $2.74 a share in 1998.
